applies_why: The judge text does not ground UNDERDETERMINED on a single verse failing to state a link or its contrary; it relies on a chain stalemate.
quote: D5 vs C1 (Acts 2:30): UNDERDETERMINED -- [CR2] and [CR3] answered the loins/seed row with Genesis 46:26 and Hebrews 7:10 (loins at depth) and the legal/flesh distinction, while [DR3] presses that the only named Davidic man is Joseph; neither chain forces the other.
rule_words: That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side.
room: single verse does not state a link or its contrary: one reading bars UNDERDETERMINED whenever a single verse does not state the link; the other bars only using that nonstatement as the ground, not a finding that two chains neither force the other.
why: The ruling rests on the judge's assessment that neither party's chain forces the other, not on a single verse's failure to state the link or its contrary.
